sentences.text: Henry Fairfield Osborn originally estimated the length of this dinosaur at 2.22 meters, while later researchers David Norman and John Foster suggested it was about 2 meters long.

Its head was proportionally smaller than most other dinosaur predators, but the skull was strongly built with a short snout and a robust lower jaw. Its eye sockets were quite large, measuring more than 25 percent of the skull length.
Ornitholestes is a coelurosaurian similar in many aspects to Compsognathus, though much longer.
Charles R. Knight's influential illustration of Ornitholestes chasing Archaeopteryx appeared in popular dinosaur books throughout the 20th century.

Ornitholestes is known from a single partial skeleton with a crushed skull found at Bone Cabin Quarry in Wyoming in 1900. All known information about Ornitholestes comes from a single specimen discovered in 1900 at the Bone Cabin Mine near Medicine Bow, Wyoming, and described by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1903.
Ornitholestes was the first theropod dinosaur discovered in the 1900s.
Ornitholestes was an agile carnivore that lived in forested habitats. Ornitholestes likely fed on lizards and mammals, though it may also have been an opportunistic scavenger.
Most recent authors suggest that Ornitholestes had a diet of small terrestrial vertebrates.
In 1903, Henry Fairfield Osborn interpreted the large conical front teeth, rapid grasping hand, and balancing tail of Ornitholestes as adaptations for preying on contemporary birds.
A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and colleagues examined 20 foot bones of Ornitholestes and found no signs of stress fractures.
When the elbow of Ornitholestes was flexed to its maximum extent, the humerus and radius formed a 53° angle.
Ornitholestes may have used its ability to bend its elbows inward to grasp prey with both hands simultaneously.

The 1996 discovery of Sinosauropteryx in China revealed a coat of rudimentary furlike feathers. John Foster inferred in 2007 that Ornitholestes likely had primitive feathers covering the body except the legs, possibly with longer feathers on the skull, neck, and forearm edges.
Ornithologist Percy Lowe proposed in 1944 that Ornitholestes might have had feathers. If present, Ornitholestes' feathers would likely have been used for insulation and possibly for incubating eggs.
All published cladistic analyses classify Ornitholestes as a coelurosaur as defined by Gauthier.
Ornitholestes is classified within the subfamily Ornitholestinae.
The genus Ornitholestes was named by Osborn in 1903.
Ornitholestes lived about 154 million years ago in the late Jurassic of what is now North America.
Ornitholestes lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 157 million years ago, from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, in what is now North America.
Ornitholestes belongs to the parent group Compsognathidae.
The hypothesis that Ornitholestes had a modified sickle claw is difficult to confirm due to poor preservation of the toe.
Oliver W.M. Rauhut and Kenneth Carpenter et al. rejected the idea of a nasal horn, attributing the bone bulge to post-mortem crushing.
Kimberley Chapelle and colleagues presented robust evidence in 2021 suggesting Ornitholestes is the earliest-diverging oviraptorosaur based on CT scan analysis of the skull.
In 2007, John Foster suggested a possible niche division between similarly sized Ornitholestes and its contemporary Coelurus.
